title: Safe first steps in AWS
idea: A new AWS account starts with a root user that has full access, billing included. Secure it, work as an administrative user, and set a budget alert.
points: The root user is the email and password you signed up with.
Multi-factor authentication (MFA) adds a second login proof, such as an app code.
IAM is AWS's users-and-permissions service. Create your administrative user there.
A cost budget alerts you when actual or forecast spend crosses your threshold.

items.label: Secure root
items.text: Sign up, then turn on MFA for the root user.

items.label: Create an admin user
items.text: Make an administrative user in IAM for everyday work.

items.label: Open Billing
items.text: Root activates IAM access to Billing. Your admin user also needs billing permissions.

items.label: Put root away
items.text: Log in as the admin user from now on. Create no root access keys.

items.label: Set a budget
items.text: Create a cost budget with an email alert before you create any resources.

items.label: Check your identity
items.text: Run `aws sts get-caller-identity` to see who the AWS CLI acts as.

code.title: Budget limit
code.caption: A monthly cost budget. Replace `<monthly-limit>` with your own number; `Unit` is a currency code.

code.title: Alert rule
code.caption: Who is told, and when. This rule emails you once spend passes the threshold.

walk.text: `ACTUAL` alerts on money already spent. A `FORECASTED` alert waits for about five weeks of usage history.
Alert when spend is greater than 80 percent of the budget amount.
Send the alert by email. An Amazon SNS topic, a notification channel, is the other option.

code.title: AWS CLI commands
code.caption: The AWS CLI is AWS's command-line tool. Run these as your admin user, never as root.

walk.text: Show who the CLI acts as. The `Arn`, your identity's full name, must not end in `:root`.
Create the budget from two JSON files: the limit, and who is alerted.

pitfalls: Avoid long-term access keys for people; AWS prefers temporary credentials (roles, IAM Identity Center).
Never commit access keys or copy them into an image; whoever reads them acts as you.
A budget alert is not a spending cap: charges can pass the threshold before it arrives.

quiz.q: Why do daily work as an administrative user instead of root?
options: Root has full access, so misuse does the most harm
Root is billed at a higher rate
Only IAM users can run the AWS CLI
quiz.why: Root has complete access, billing included. Keep it for the few tasks that need it, with MFA on.

takeaway: Lock root with MFA, work as an admin user, and set a budget.
